gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the three Nebula picks on one footing: ProjectorCentral's measured lumens in Movie mode (X1 2,193; Cosmos 4K SE 1,298; Mars 3 686) against their 3,500/1,800/1,000 ANSI claims. None says that the Mars 3's 5-hour battery claim is for Eco mode, where Movie mode measured 261 lumens. None says that the outlet-only X1 draws about 160 W at full brightness, roughly 0.3 kWh for a 2-hour film, so it can also run from a portable power station.
standout_why: Wirecutter (cited, via proxy) measured the Mars 3 at 'over 800 lumens' maximum, 'over 600' in Custom mode, about 2 h at 100% and 4 h 45 min in Eco at 20% brightness. It gives no lumen figure for the X1 or Cosmos 4K SE and does not tie the Eco runtime to a lumen number. ChatGPT's answer repeats the makers' 3,500/1,800/1,000 ANSI and 3,200 ISO numbers side by side, with only a note that ISO and ANSI ratings aren't interchangeable. It says the X1 'Requires AC power' and says nothing about power draw. I could not read the cited RTINGS pages (outdoor list, X1 review, portable list) because WebFetch returned only navigation, and curl was blocked by permissions. RTINGS may publish its own measured brightness for the X1, which is why this scores 2 and not 3. Yahoo returned 403 and Forbes was not opened.
decides: Confirms the X1 as the brightness pick: it measures about 1.7x the Cosmos 4K SE and about 3.2x the Mars 3 in Movie mode. It also weakens 'Mars 3 if you have no outlet' as a reason to give up brightness. At about 160 W, the X1 should run a 2-hour film from a 1 kWh-class power station, which the site already lists (e.g. Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2, BLUETTI Elite 100 V2). Mars 3 buyers should plan on Standard power (about 2 h, about 686–959 lumens), not the 5-hour Eco figure, if they want a 100-inch-plus picture.

findings.label: Claimed brightness
findings.note: Maker spec page. The projector has no battery and a DC-IN input with an external adapter. The page lists no rated power draw.

findings.label: Measured brightness, Movie mode (SDR)
findings.source_title: ProjectorCentral, Anker Nebula X1 Smart 4K Portable Projector Review (Nikki Kahl, 2025-08-19)
findings.note: 100% brightness, Max Iris, 9-sector average. Standard measured 2,588, and the brightest mode (Conference) measured 3,187, which is 91% of claim. 2,193 / 3,500 = 63%.

findings.label: Measured power draw at highest brightness
findings.source_title: Notebookcheck, Nebula X1 practical test (Marcus Schwarten, 2025-08-02, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Notebookcheck writes '160 Wh', which must mean watts, since it also says a 2-hour film takes 'a good 0.3 kWh'. Our arithmetic: 160 W × 2 h = 0.32 kWh. A 1,024 Wh station at an assumed 85% inverter efficiency gives about 870 Wh / 160 W ≈ 5.4 h. That runtime is our estimate, not a measurement.

findings.label: Claimed vs measured brightness
findings.value: 1,800 ANSI claimed; 1,800 measured in Conference, 1,298 in Movie (72%)
findings.source_title: ProjectorCentral, Anker Nebula Cosmos 4K SE Smart Projector Review (Nikki Kahl, 2024-11-29)
findings.note: Other modes measured: Standard 1,426, NebulaMaster 1,355, Game and Sport 1,334, Vivid 1,305. No built-in battery. Netflix is preloaded on Google TV with no dongle. 1,298 / 1,800 = 72%.

findings.label: Claimed brightness and runtime per power mode
findings.value: 1,000 ANSI lumens; Eco mode lowers brightness to 300 lumens for the 5 h battery claim; 185 Wh battery
findings.source_title: soundcore Nebula Mars 3 | Outdoor Projector with 5H Long Playtime
findings.note: The spec table lists 'Battery Life (Eco Mode) 5 Hrs'. The page gives no runtime for Standard mode. Bundles were priced at $1,049.99 on the US page on the read date. 40 W speakers, IPX3, 19 V / 9.47 A adapter (about 180 W by arithmetic).

findings.label: Measured brightness by picture and power mode
findings.value: Bright/Standard power 959; Movie/Standard power 686; Movie/Eco 261; Bright/Eco 442 lumens
findings.note: ANSI measurements. With AI power mode at 70%, Movie measured 388. The review does not say whether it measured on AC or battery. It quotes Anker's 2 h for Standard and 5 h for Eco. 686 / 1,000 = 69%; 261 / 1,000 = 26%.

findings.label: Measured battery runtime (rival reference)
findings.value: about 2 h at 100% brightness; 4 h 45 min in Eco at 20% brightness
findings.source_title: Wirecutter, The 7 Best Projectors of 2026 (cited by ChatGPT)
findings.note: Wirecutter measured 'over 800 lumens' maximum and 'over 600' in Custom mode. This finding is already on a cited page and is included for comparison only.

Nebula X1 rated power consumption: the seenebula.com spec page lists DC-IN but no wattage. A 240 W figure appears only on retailer listings with a near-match model number. No manual was found.
Mars 3 brightness on battery vs AC: neither the soundcore page nor ProjectorCentral says whether Standard-mode output drops when running on battery.
RTINGS measured brightness for the X1, Mars 3 and Cosmos 4K SE: all three cited RTINGS pages rendered only navigation in WebFetch, and curl was blocked by permissions.
